five.t: **Democrats take both chambers,** flipping seven Senate seats. Friday's Europe posture options and the lame-duck defence bill come before the new majority sits.
**The fridge attacks reach Kaiserslautern;** two former US officials tell NPR some evidence points to Iran.
**EUCOM tells troops and families to vary their routines** under a new theatre-wide security campaign.
**Abu Dhabi is set for 10–11 Nov, security arrangements first;** Ukraine's backers meet at the European Commission today.
**Koalicja grows to 11 nations and the Netherlands joins** the first rehearsal of a post-ceasefire force for Ukraine, in Poland from 9 Nov.

pick.t: If you read one thing: the EUCOM security campaign, and what it asks of your family.

items.h: Talks get a date, a place and an agenda
items.body: Envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov: “Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace.” Vladimir Medinsky leads Russia's delegation. [12] In Berlin on 3 Nov President Zelensky listed Ukraine's aims: an energy and infrastructure ceasefire, an unblocked Black Sea and “ideally an all-for-all exchange” of prisoners. [13] Overnight into 4 Nov Russia launched 310 drones, of which 272 were shot down or suppressed by 08:00, the Air Force says; on 3 Nov drones hit a substation serving the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant. [14, 15] Zaporizhzhia police put the toll of the 2 Nov bombing of an underground school used for aid handouts in Komyshuvakha at 37, with 59 people missing. [16]
items.next: Technical talks at the European Commission today; a White House event on an Oleshky ceasefire on Thu 5 Nov; Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov; the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin on 19 Nov. [17, 18, 19]

items.h: Qatar waits on both capitals; a sailor dies off Oman
items.body: Qatari mediators took a draft to Tehran on 2 Nov and await answers from both sides within 36 hours. Spokesman Majed al-Ansari: “If there were no glimmer of hope, there would be no negotiations.” Mohsen Rezaei of Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the US response “was not convincing”, and President Trump told Fox News: “If we have to, we'll have to.” [20] India says the dhow Al Jusufi was attacked near Limah, Oman, killing one Indian seafarer. [21]
items.next: Qatar's 36-hour window runs to about 5 Nov; no date is set for direct talks. [20]

items.h: Democrats take both chambers and flip seven Senate seats
items.body: CBS projected Democratic control of the House at 22:15 ET on 3 Nov; by 04:47 ET NBC News projected at least 258 Democratic seats, the most since 1993. [22, 23] Democrats flipped seven Republican Senate seats: Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas, where James Talarico beat Ken Paxton. [24] Alaska and Mississippi were still uncalled on Wednesday morning; in Mississippi Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 28 votes at about 01:00 ET with about 97% counted. [25, 23] Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer: “against all odds, we Democrats have won the Senate.” [26] President Trump: “I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran.” [23]
items.next: Counting goes on in Alaska and Mississippi; the lame-duck Congress returns on 9 Nov and the new Congress sits on 3 Jan 2027. [25, 27]

items.h: North Korea fires again; Taiwan counts 49 sorties
items.body: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff say North Korea fired “several missiles” from the Sondok area of South Hamgyong toward the East Sea on 4 Nov, the fourth launch event in a week; type and range were not given. [28] Kim Yo Jong said in a statement carried by the state agency KCNA that talks with Washington are possible but not a necessity. [29] Taiwan's defence ministry logged 49 Chinese military aircraft sorties, six warships and six government vessels in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 4 Nov. [30]
items.next: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov. [30]

items.h: Sudan counts drones from Ethiopia; Uvira marches
items.body: Sudan's government says 187 drones in 70 attacks came from Ethiopian territory from February to October, 97 of them in October, killing 176 soldiers and 484 civilians; Ethiopia denies it. [31] In Goma the head of the UN mission (MONUSCO) met Joseph Kabila, leader of a rebel coalition that includes M23; its vice-president Bertrand Bisimwa said “one more mandate would change absolutely nothing”. [32] More than 100,000 people marched for peace in Uvira on 4 Nov. [33]
items.next: MONUSCO's mandate expires in December; Sudan's complaints sit with the UN Security Council and the African Union, with no session date published. [32, 31]

feature.title: Russia's drone war by the month: November to September
body: The Institute for Science and International Security adds up the Ukrainian Air Force's daily reports into monthly totals of Shahed-type drones, decoys included. Its series runs from 5,447 in November 2025 to a low of 4,442 in January, then climbs to 6,462 in March and 6,583 in April before a peak of 8,161 in May. June fell to 5,749 and July to 4,981; August reached 5,166. For September the institute counts 6,732 as a reporting baseline and estimates the full month at 7,400 to 7,700. [34]

AFP's monthly counts of the same reports run close: 5,445 drones in November and 8,150 in May. [35, 36] AFP's missile counts move on a different rhythm: 215 in November, 211 in May and 376 in July, 126 of them ballistic. [35, 36, 37]

October has no single total yet. On 2 Nov Air Force spokesman Yurii Ihnat gave “more than 4,000 jet-powered UAVs” and “4,740 conventional drones”, with “around 150 ballistic missiles” and “80 cruise and air-launched missiles”. [38] On 3 Nov the General Staff counted 6,473 Shahed-131, Shahed-136 and Shahed-238 drones launched and 4,859 destroyed, with 66% of jet-powered drones and 89% of conventional ones intercepted. [39] The two figures count different things, so the chart stops at September.
after: Drone figures from the institute's Table 1a; missile figures from AFP's monthly analyses for the months shown. [34]

incidents.text: Police confirmed a food-processing firm and a supermarket hit, in the district of the US Kaiserslautern Military Community. [40]
Cooling set to about 30 °C; the owner puts the loss above €360,000. A market in Wetter-Volmarstein was also hit. [40]
Thirteen SuperValu stores among more than 100 hit in Europe; Estonia, Luxembourg and Finland also report cases. [41]
A drone the military believes was Ukrainian crashed and has not been found; NATO jets were scrambled. [42]
Latvia's military now assesses the drone as a Russian Geran-type, armed status unclear, that flew back into Russia. [42]

leads.title: The fridge wave reaches Kaiserslautern, and investigators look at Iran
leads.teaser: Police confirm two sites in the US military community's home district, and two former US officials tell NPR some evidence points to Iran.
rows: Westpfalz police confirmed that a food-processing firm and a supermarket in the Kaiserslautern and Kusel districts were hit; dpa adds Lilienthal and Wetter-Volmarstein. [40] SecurityWeek counts more than 100 stores, 13 of them in Ireland. [41]

dpa says the attack went through the firm that maintains the systems remotely; Censys counts just over 1,000 internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView interfaces. [40, 41] The Fort Irwin and Fort Huachuca commissaries use Danfoss remote controls. [43]

A0 in Europe; Belgium's cyber centre says “it may never be possible to identify” the attacker. [44] Two former US officials told NPR some evidence points to Iran, without high confidence; DCIS and Army CID's Cyber Field Office work with French police. [43]
Israel's cyber directorate told chains to “immediately inspect” remote refrigeration controls; Commissioner Hansen called the repeat attacks “deeply concerning”. [45, 41]
leads.sw: Kaiserslautern is where US reinforcements are received and fed: ask the J4 whether contracted cold storage there and in the Benelux has changed default passwords and cut remote access, and who checks.

leads.title: Latvia: one Russian drone, one Ukrainian, in two days
leads.teaser: The military calls the 1 Nov intruder a Russian Geran-type that flew back; a second drone on 2 Nov, probably Ukrainian, crashed and is still missing.
rows: Latvia's military assesses the 1 Nov drone as a Russian Geran-type, armed status unclear, that flew back; the 2 Nov drone, probably Ukrainian, crashed inside Latvia and has not been found. [42]
NATO air-policing jets were scrambled and residents near the border told to shelter. [42]
leads.sw: A crashed, unfound drone is a search, explosive-ordnance and evidence task at once: check which national agency leads it in each Baltic state.

pattern: **Through the maintainer:** dpa traces the German cases to the firm that services the controllers remotely, as Portugal's were traced to a contractor. [40]
**Military communities in range:** Kaiserslautern joins the US commissary outages, and two US commissaries run the same vendor's remote controls. [40, 43]
**Drones from both sides over the Baltic:** Latvia logged a Russian and a Ukrainian drone on consecutive days. [42]

DCIS and Army CID work with French police on the commissary intrusions
Italy reissues its refrigeration bulletin; Sweden's NCSC shares data with Nordic and EU partners
Latvia scrambles NATO air policing and names the 1 Nov drone as Russian

hybrid.note: Within 100 km of Heerlen there is no confirmed case: Delhaize says small stores in Flanders and Wallonia were hit without naming them, and Dutch victims are not named. [44, 46]

europe.h: Poland's council backs a US base; the answer sits in Washington
europe.body: The closed National Security Council on 3 Nov took no formal decision. Prime Minister Donald Tusk spoke of a “bardzo szeroki konsensus”, a very broad consensus; the president's aide Marcin Przydacz warned the window “być może nie będzie trwało wiecznie”, may not last forever. [47, 48] Defence24 reported that Pentagon talks are due in mid-November and a decision in December, for about 5,000 permanent troops at a Polish cost of PLN 15–17 billion. [49]
europe.sw: A paid-for permanent base in Poland is the cheapest yes in the posture review; the Benelux and German garrisons are the comparison.

europe.h: Posture options reach Hegseth on Friday
europe.body: At least four option sets on US force levels in Europe are due to Hegseth by 6 Nov, with the review complete in December. [50] John Deni of the Army War College counts about 65,000 accompanied and 15,000 rotational troops and puts rehousing 15,000 to 25,000 in the United States at $8 billion or more; Congress requires a plan before numbers fall below 76,000. [51] A Defense News opinion piece argues Spain could lose some of Rota's six destroyers. [52]
europe.sw: The options arrive two months before a Democratic House can question them.

euregio.h: A4 toward Köln: a junction tonight, one lane Thursday night
euregio.body: The Weisweiler junction is closed toward Köln from 19:00 tonight to 05:00; from 19:00 Thursday to 05:00 Friday two of three lanes close between Eschweiler-West and Eschweiler-Ost toward Köln. [8] The Aachen-Zentrum ramps toward the Netherlands stay shut until about 13 Nov. [53]
euregio.fy: Through traffic from Heerlen is unaffected tonight; on Thursday night allow extra time east of Eschweiler.

euregio.h: Maastricht University cancels a lecture on safety grounds
euregio.body: The university cancelled “Drie jaar na 7 oktober”, a lecture organised by IJAR and StandWithUs, citing safety; the organisers say the university “zwicht voor intimidatie”, gives in to intimidation. [54]

euregio.h: Fake police officers in Heerlen and Maastricht
euregio.body: Police arrested a 22-year-old Heerlen woman, recognised from released footage, for defrauding a 72-year-old while posing as an officer; on Tuesday evening a reported robbery on the Heerderweg in Maastricht turned out to be another fake-officer case. [55, 56]
euregio.fy: Real police never collect bank cards, cash or jewellery at the door; check by calling 0900-8844.

P.L. 119-103 bars new starts and production-rate increases. [58]
Seven Senate seats flipped; Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled. [24, 25]

words.role: Commander, US European Command, and Supreme Allied Commander Europe
words.where: Written statement launching EUCOM's “See Something, Do Something” campaign
words.quote: Our personnel and their families are our most precious asset, and their safety is our highest priority.
words.context: Released on 2 Nov and reported on 3 Nov, launching a theatre-wide security campaign. [60]

words.quote: Netanyahu and I, we made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year.
words.context: CBS reports he said the aid would end this year. [61]

words.quote: I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran.
words.context: Logged at 01:38 ET on 4 Nov as the results came in; he also said he was “a little bit surprised”. [23]

depth.kind: Wednesday · An acquisition programme in numbers
depth.title: ERAM: a thousand cruise missiles in fifteen months
body: The Extended Range Attack Munition (ERAM) is a cheap air-launched cruise missile the Air Force buys for Ukraine. On 3 Nov it asked industry for more than 1,000, the first within three months of award and all within 15; replies are due 19 Nov. The specification: 500-pound class, more than 250 nautical miles, faster than Mach 0.6, within 10 metres with GPS degraded. [59]

The 2024 requirement was 1,000 in 24 months, about 42 a month; the new one implies about 67, some 60% faster. [62] A 2025 sale of up to 3,350 ERAMs for $825 million, paid by Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway with US financing, works out at about $246,000 a round with support; no official unit cost is published. [63] A PAC-3 interceptor in the sale cleared for Ukraine on 2 Nov costs about $4.2 million. [64]

dod.h: EUCOM tells troops and families to vary their routines
dod.body: Gen. Grynkewich launched a theatre-wide “See Something, Do Something” campaign on 2 Nov, asking personnel and families to vary routines and report anything suspicious; EUCOM will not discuss force protection levels. Last month 12 B-1 bombers left RAF Fairford after warnings of Iran-backed attacks. [60]
dod.sw: Expect it in the US element's briefings at JFC Brunssum and in the next force protection review.
dod.fy: Vary the school run and the commute this month, and agree with the children what to report and to whom.

dod.h: The Pentagon follows Ukraine into ground robots
dod.body: Defense One counts more than $115 million for unmanned ground vehicles in FY2026, against more than 22,000 ground robots Ukraine ordered from January to July; the 75th Ranger Regiment and the Marines are buying more than a dozen Overland AI IBEX vehicles for about $25 million. [65] AUTOWARCOM still needs legislation; NBC reported that the Defense Innovation Unit's director, Owen West, would lead it at first. [66]
dod.sw: The US buys ground robots by the dozen and Ukraine by the thousand; allied logistics will meet Ukrainian-style robots first.

dod.h: Special operations gets a space component and a modular missile
dod.body: The Space Force activated its component to US Special Operations Command on 2 Nov, SOCOM's first new service component since 2006, with space special warfare teams aligned to the theatre special operations commands. [67] On 3 Nov SOCOM gave Aeon Industrial $13.8 million for fewer than 100 shoulder-fired Zeus missiles with field-swappable warheads. [68]
dod.sw: Ask how SOCEUR's space team will route requests for space effects to the NATO joint force commands.

news.h: Former Army Secretary Driscoll joins OpenAI
news.body: Dan Driscoll, who drove the Army Transformation Initiative as Secretary, joins OpenAI as “senior counselor for national security modernization”; his old post is still held by an acting secretary. [69, 70]
news.sw: Another transformation author moves to a frontier lab; expect closer ties between OpenAI and Army acquisition.

congress.h: The election hands both chambers to Democrats; the lame duck starts 9 Nov
congress.body: Neither chamber sat. Democrats won the House and flipped seven Senate seats, so both Armed Services committees change hands when the new Congress sits on 3 Jan 2027. [24, 23] Until then the FY2027 defence bill (H.R. 8800) and the 11 Dec funding deadline fall to the lame-duck session from 9 Nov, and Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral's nomination to US Army Europe and Africa (PN1188) waits on the Executive Calendar as No. 924. [71, 57]
congress.sw: The posture options reach Hegseth on Friday and the current chairs write the lame-duck NDAA; from January new chairs can question both, including the 76,000-troop floor.

items.h: TRICARE Young Adult premiums up 11% on average in 2027
items.body: Open Season runs 9 Nov to 8 Dec with changes from 1 Jan; premiums for TRICARE Young Adult, for adult children up to 26, rise by an average 11%. [72, 73]
items.fy: Doing nothing keeps the family's current plan.

items.h: 2027 TSP limits not out yet
items.body: The IRS still lists the 2026 limits: $24,500 in deferrals and $8,000 catch-up. A Milliman projection reported by Forbes puts 2027 at $25,500, a forecast rather than an IRS figure. [74, 75]
items.fy: Wait for the IRS notice before resetting January contributions.

dates: TRICARE and Federal Benefits open seasons open
2027 pay raise and benefit changes take effect
career.note: The 2027 raise is still 7-6-5 in the House bills and 3.6% in the Senate's. [76]

items.h: Koalicja grows to 11 nations, and the Netherlands joins
items.body: London and Paris put Koalicja 26.2 at about 2,800 personnel from 11 nations around Nowa Dęba from 9 to 22 Nov: France 1,100, Britain 300 plus Typhoons and a tanker, and Türkiye clearing mines from Istanbul; drones and counter-drone kit, no tanks. [77, 78] The commander, Lt Gen Tom Bateman: “It is not designed for offensive operations.” [77] The Dutch ministry says the Netherlands joins “op korte termijn”, at short notice; a role in the force itself needs a political decision. [79] Poland's figure of almost 2,000 Polish soldiers does not fit the total. [80]
items.sw: Check which Dutch units drawn into Koalicja are also offered to the NATO Force Model.

items.h: Germany: the Boxer mega-order slips; Slovenia joins the IRIS-T circle
items.body: The trade site hartpunkt reports that the Arminius order, just over €20 billion for about 1,800 Boxers including Skyranger air defence and RCH 155 howitzers, now comes no earlier than February 2027; the ministry declined to comment. [81] Slovenia, with three IRIS-T SLM fire units on order, agreed closer cooperation with Defence Minister Boris Pistorius on 3 Nov; Germany aims for 3.5% of GDP on core defence in 2029. [82]
items.sw: Skyranger air defence for German manoeuvre brigades slips with the Boxer order.

items.h: Baltic leaders: rebuild fast, and call hybrid attacks kinetic
items.body: Estonia's Defence Minister Martin Herem took additions to the defence plan, unapproved since January, to the National Defence Council; one option trades missiles for aircraft and air-to-air systems. Herem: “we need to develop certain capabilities very quickly.” [83] Lithuania's President Gitanas Nausėda called “hybrid threats” a “convenient euphemism”: “some of the recent attacks in essence are kinetic attacks.” [84]
items.sw: Expect the kinetic framing in Article 4 debates on the plans JFC Brunssum owns.

items.h: Saab flies its own AI agents on a Gripen E
items.body: Saab says an AI agent “autonomously controlled the aircraft” in beyond-visual-range combat scenarios on Gripen E flight trials, after training over “millions of simulated flight hours”; no flight count or dates were given. [85]
items.sw: Allied air planners will meet an AI pilot in exercises before doctrine catches up.

items.h: Kyiv wires hundreds of sites against remote-piloted Shaheds
items.body: Defense Express, citing an unnamed report, says jammers went up at “hundreds of locations” in Kyiv within weeks to cut the radio links Russian operators use to steer jet-powered Shaheds, and that Russia paused the method. [86] Ukraine's border guards say they destroyed 73 Russian ambush drones in October. [87]
items.sw: City-scale jamming is a defence no NATO capital has rehearsed.

items.h: STARK shows a 24-metre strike drone boat
items.body: The German start-up STARK unveiled Vanta 24 at Euronaval, an uncrewed boat for anti-ship missiles and its Cascade loitering munition, with autonomy that works under satellite-navigation jamming; FSG will build it, and no customer is named. [88] MBDA showed DELUGE, a missile “designed for large-scale production”. [89]
items.sw: Expect drone boats on both sides in Baltic and North Sea planning.

aperture.contrarian: Europe reads a Democratic Congress as a brake on troop cuts, but the options reach Hegseth on Friday and the new Congress sits only on 3 Jan. [50, 27] The case for the brake: Congress already requires a plan before numbers fall below 76,000. [51]
aperture.weak: Kaiserslautern. Confirmation that it was chosen rather than swept up: a hit on a contractor supplying US facilities, or a German statement linking it to the commissary cases. [40, 43]

number.t: Internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView refrigeration interfaces counted by Censys worldwide, most in France, then Belgium and the US. [41]

aperture.inject: STARTEX + 5, 03:10. Two host-nation cold stores supplying a US reception site near Kaiserslautern report freezers at +25 °C; the maintainer's remote portal shows logins from an unknown address. Stresses baseline requirements 4 (food and water) and 7 (transport). First call: the contracting officer, to shut the portal.
aperture.question: Which contractors hold remote access to systems serving NATO and US sites in our area, and can we cut that access at night without the vendor?

deep.title: Koalicja, seen from Moscow
body: Read Koalicja as a Russian planner would. It runs 9–22 Nov, and the Abu Dhabi talks on 10–11 Nov put “post-war security arrangements” first. [77, 12] A force rehearsing its deployment while that clause is negotiated gives Moscow a reason to slow the clause, or to price its concessions higher.

To a Russian staff officer a light force of about 2,800 with no tanks, “not designed for offensive operations”, is a test of will rather than a threat: its worth rests on whether its governments would reinforce it once struck. [77] Its seams, 11 nations, no NATO flag and a Polish troop figure that does not fit the total, are openings for messaging aimed at the parliaments that must vote the deployment. [80]

longread.title: A new cold war: hackers target fridges across the globe
longread.why: Jenna McLaughlin on the commissary investigation and the Danfoss contracts. [43]

items.h: AMD ships MI450 and Helios; data-centre sales nearly double
items.body: AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, up about 45%, with data-centre sales of $8.5 billion, up 97%, and guided about $17 billion for the fourth quarter. It says the MI450 launched in the quarter and that Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud are running models on the first Helios rack systems; ROCm 10 is released, and a space-grade Versal chip rated for 15-year missions is sampling. [90] Shares rose about 8% after hours. [91]

items.h: Google DeepMind gives its coding agent chemistry skills
items.body: Google DeepMind released Cheminformatics Skills for its Antigravity agent on 3 Nov, built on the RDKit toolkit with links to the ChEMBL and PubChem databases. In its demonstration the agent curated 568 compounds and benchmarked machine-learning models across four experimental readouts in about an hour; Google offers 10,000 scientists the top tier free for six months and warns that “computational designs are testable hypotheses, not finished drugs.” [92]

items.h: Baidu's world model drives 100,000 simulated km a day
items.body: Baidu launched Apollo World on 3 Nov, an AI model that simulates road environments and generates up to 100,000 km of driving a day, which Baidu equates to about three years of real-world testing with a safety driver; it already trains the Apollo Go robotaxi fleet. [93]

Brent swung more than $6 on conflicting Iran signals before settling at $103.60, and Dutch gas fell to its lowest in over a week. [98, 99] Closes are from Yahoo Finance. [94]

items.h: Tax plan debate today: a Kamer majority in sight, no Senate deal
items.body: ChristenUnie and 50Plus are positive about the third version of the 2027 tax plan, and with Groep Markuszower, which calls a vote against childish, the cabinet has a majority in the Tweede Kamer. JA21, BBB and SGP still want to tie their votes to asylum, nitrogen and abortion, which the cabinet refuses; CDA leader Henri Bontenbal will meet other party leaders next week. 50Plus calls the Eerste Kamer, which takes the plan in December, a major risk. [5]
items.fy: The vote is Thursday 12 Nov; until then the fuel-duty discount for 2027 is not settled. [5]

items.h: Dutch inflation rises to 3.7% in October
items.body: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) puts October inflation at 3.7%, up from 3.4% in September; prices rose 0.7% in the month. Energy including motor fuels cost 14.4% more than a year earlier, while food, drink and tobacco were 0.6% cheaper. On the EU measure the rate is 3.3%, and the full figures follow on 10 Nov. [6]
items.fy: Energy drives the rise: if your energy contract is variable, compare fixed offers before the cold months.

items.h: What version three changes
items.body: Besides scrapping the €347 million defence levy for 2027 and delaying box 3 to 2029, the plan cuts the box 2 rates from 24.5% to 23.5% and from 31% to 29%, keeps a narrower deduction for specific healthcare costs with €350 million a year, postpones the VAT rise on flowers and plants, and adds €95 million for police and prosecutors. Prime Minister Rob Jetten says purchasing power is €1.5 billion better than on Budget Day. [104, 105]
items.fy: Keep receipts for medical costs: the deduction survives in narrower form. [105]

items.h: Bus unions advise a no; strikes possible from 17 Nov
items.body: FNV and CNV advise members to reject the employers' final offer of 2% backdated to 1 July and 4% in 2027; members vote in the week of 9 Nov, and actions could start from 17 Nov at Arriva, Keolis, Qbuzz, Transdev and EBS. NS is not covered. [106]
items.fy: Arriva's Limburg staff sat out October's strikes under a separate contract; check before relying on a bus from 17 Nov. [106]

nl.temp: Warm. A Kamer majority now looks within reach with CU, 50Plus and Markuszower; the Eerste Kamer in December is the harder test.

items.h: Sint-Hubertus feasts in Tongeren from Thursday
items.body: The Hubertus festivities at the Offelken racecourse run 5–12 Nov, a living heritage tradition with a procession and blessings; free, about 40 minutes away. [108]

items.h: A children's castle tour at Kasteel Hoensbroek on Sunday
items.body: Het Kasteel in rep en roer! runs at 11:30 and 13:30 on Sun 8 Nov for ages 4 to 7, lasts 60 minutes and is included in regular admission. It cannot be booked ahead: sign up at the cashier on the day, 10 minutes before the start, in groups of up to 10 children. About 5 minutes away. [109]

items.h: GLOW lights up Eindhoven from Saturday
items.body: The light-art festival's walking route of about 5 km starts at Eindhoven Centraal and runs nightly 18:30–23:00 from 7 to 14 Nov; entry is free. About 55 minutes away. [110]

otd.title: On this day · 4 November 1944
otd.body: At about 11:00 the German 116th Panzer and 89th Infantry Divisions attacked Schmidt from three sides and retook it from the 112th Infantry of the US 28th Infantry Division, a day after the Americans had captured it; the survivors held on at Kommerscheidt. Their only supply route was the Kall trail, which tanks could barely use. The division lost 6,184 men in eight days, and Schmidt, about 40 km from Heerlen, stayed in German hands until February 1945. [122]

culture.title: Sint Maarten, next Wednesday
culture.body: On 11 November children walk with paper lanterns and sing door to door for sweets. The custom long survived only in the northern provinces, North Holland above the IJ and Limburg; around Venlo children carried lanterns to a Sint-Maartensvuur, a bonfire, and families ate kerneelkes, sweet waffles. [123]

flags: Reissue: this edition was first published at 05:47 CET in the 5.0 format and reissued at 13:00 in the 6.0 format, with the same number and date. Added since the first issue: the Senate result, the Dutch and euro-area October inflation flashes, the overnight drone attack on Ukraine and the Komyshuvakha toll. Senate and House control rest on NBC, CBS and CNBC projections; no AP call on control was found. Single-source or thin: the Kaiserslautern, Kusel, Lilienthal and Wetter-Volmarstein cases (dpa via WirtschaftsWoche); the Irish, Estonian, Luxembourg and Finnish counts (SecurityWeek); the Iran evidence for the commissary outages (two former officials, NPR); Kyiv's electronic-warfare shield (Defense Express, citing an unnamed report); the Boxer order delay (hartpunkt; the ministry declined comment); the White House Oleshky event (Ukrinform, citing a source); Defence24's December timeline for the Polish base. Polish and Dutch quotes are translated in the text; Tusk's and Przydacz's words are as printed by Defence24 and Polsat News. Grynkewich's statement is dated 2 Nov and was first reported on 3 Nov. Koalicja: Poland's ministry speaks of almost 2,000 Polish soldiers, which does not square with the 2,800 total given by London and Paris. Not in the window: no remarks from Hegseth, Caine, Telle or LaNeve; nothing new on strategy or force design; the posture options had not leaked; Congress did not sit. Frontier: Investing.com reported Tencent's full Hy4 release on 4 Nov without published numbers, so it is left out; no other release dated 3–4 Nov was found. Career: the colonel board recess date rests on a mirror of MILPER 26-170 (HRC's own page needs a login), so it stays as a career date, not an item. Out and about: the Phantasialand and Aachen circus picks of the first issue rested on event listings only and were swapped for the Kasteel Hoensbroek and GLOW picks; both stay in the event list. World feature: trimmed to six sources, so the AFP missile counts show November, May and July only. Ukraine data: the Air Force tally for the night of 3–4 Nov (310 drones, 272 downed or suppressed by 08:00; Ukrinform's summary lists no missiles) and minfin's 4 Nov row (+2,180 personnel, +1,104 drones) were appended; no Air Force tally for the night of 2–3 Nov was found, so ua-air has no 3 Nov row. October has no single drone total: the Air Force and the General Staff count different things, so the Trend line stops at September. Not reached: war.gov, defense.gov contracts and congress.gov web pages (nomination data via api.congress.gov), De Limburger, Aachener Zeitung, Het Belang van Limburg and WDR; the AFNORTH calendar PDF returned 403, so the rows are carried from the 3 Nov check. Data checks: the ECB history ZIP's latest fix is 3 Nov (1.1179 dollars per euro, USD/EUR 0.8945), already in fx.json; today's fix comes about 16:00. Yahoo closes for 3 Nov are in series.json; canes.json matches the NHL standings (12-3-2, 26 points, first in the Metro). The Open-Meteo snow forecast was refreshed for all 12 resorts (no snow depth above 2 cm). Source rows in standing files that the edition does not cite carry their own numbers.
